paragraphs: Friend, Solomon had it ALL. Gold by the year, a throne like nothing ever made for any kingdom, and kings lining up to see him. But look at WHY they came. They came "to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart." (2 Chronicles 9:23) Solomon's wisdom wasn't something he cooked up himself. It was put there by God.

Then the passage ends the way every life ends. Forty years on the throne (2 Chronicles 9:30), and then he "rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David." (2 Chronicles 9:31) Twelve thousand horses, and not one of them could follow him out of that story. I think that's the quiet punchline here. The gold stayed, and his son Rehoboam took the seat.

So here's my big idea, baker. Riches and a big name look impressive, but they don't last, and the thing worth wanting is what God puts in your heart. I got picked up for 25 cents, and what mattered was never the price sticker. It was who held me and what He gave me to do. Soak in the Word, because that's the kind of wealth you can't leave behind in a stable.
